audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 fits a 48.3% Aurora win rate over 323 games — he owns levels 1 and 4-5 and the two-item stage, she owns level 6, and the rest is skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item stage was graded as an Aurora spike in both layers even though the packet chart calls it Skill, and no cooldown numbers appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s, Riptide is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Titan’s Wrath is a flat 12s, Depth Charge is 120/100/80s. His first tank item blunts the poke spike, which is why first item is a wash rather than her window.
audit.corrected: First item flipped to Skill and the spike text rewritten around the real hook cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says three separate times that Aurora pokes him from outside Dredge Line range — spikes[2], wants.you[0] and whys[5]. Dredge Line has 1150 range; Twofold Hex has 900. She cannot outrange the hook. Staggering Blow is also never explained beyond the phrase "passive root chain".
audit.why: Riot’s data: Dredge Line 1150 range, Twofold Hex 900. Standing at your own max range still leaves you 250 units inside his hook. The right advice is to bait or sidestep it on its 14s rank-1 cooldown, not to trust spacing. Staggering Blow roots on his FIRST attack against a target, so the root is guaranteed on the opening auto, not a chain.
audit.corrected: All three range claims rewritten with the real numbers; report[5] and dontsFull[1] now state Staggering Blow correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Skill/Skill/Aurora/Aurora, giving Aurora the two-item stage in a matchup she loses, and contradicting six of the seven content whys.
audit.why: The packet chart, identical on the aurora and nautilus packets, is Nautilus/Skill/Skill/Nautilus/Aurora/Skill/Nautilus — which is what whys[0], [1], [2], [3], [4] and [6] already describe.
audit.corrected: All seven tokens flipped as one atomic group in both layers, with every phase why rewritten to match.

edits.before: Q-E weave stacks your passive drain from range. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: He walks up under Titan’s Wrath and threatens a Dredge Line hook into the Staggering Blow root before you have W to escape.

edits.before: The hop makes your poke pattern untouchable. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Twofold Hex and your passive sustain come online, but his shield and hook keep level 2 genuinely even.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your range.
edits.after: You can poke and disengage with Q and The Weirding, yet one landed Dredge Line still flips the whole trade.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His shield-poke and the standing hook threat let him walk you down every time Across the Veil’s 22s cooldown is exposed.

edits.before: Between the Worlds zones the whole all-in — fights inside it are yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Between Worlds makes you untargetable to him from outside the rift — slip the hook, ignore Depth Charge, and burst him inside it.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Your Riftmaker spike sharpens the poke, but his first tank item soaks most of it.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items of tank shrug off your poke, and he chains the Riptide slow into Depth Charge whenever your W is down.

edits.before: His only engage. W-blink it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 1150 range, 14s at rank 1 — it outreaches your Q. Bait it, then step up.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto on you, chaining into Riptide.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. W-blink it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dredge Line: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1 and 1150 range, longer than your Q. Sidestep or W out. - Riptide: 5s at rank 5, never stand in the waves. - Between Worlds: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. W-blink it. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Dredge Line reaches 1150, past your 900 Q. Staggering Blow roots on his first auto — never melee him.

edits.before: Luden's/Malignance sharpens your Twofold Hex so you chip his huge HP bar from max range, well outside Dredge Line's hook distance where he can never trade back.
edits.after: Luden’s/Malignance sharpens your Twofold Hex, but his 1150-range Dredge Line outreaches your 900 Q — chip only while the hook sits on its 12s cooldown.

edits.before: Poke with the Twofold Hex missile-and-pull from max range so his Dredge Line hook and Titan's Wrath on-hit never reach you
edits.after: Poke at your 900 max range and sidestep the hook — Dredge Line reaches 1150, so distance alone never keeps you safe

edits.before: Your Luden's/Malignance poke spike lets you stack Twofold Hex damage on his HP bar from outside Dredge Line range.
edits.after: Your Luden’s/Malignance poke chips him from range, but his first tank item soaks it and the 1150 hook still reaches you.

notes: Both packet suspectNames ("Dredge Line’s", "Your Spirit Abjuration") are FALSE POSITIVES — the names match the kit files exactly. The real defect was the range claim, not a name. Champion-level items again: "Between the Worlds" in phases[4].why and breakdown.late should be "Between Worlds", and the boilerplate "you are a immobile drain bot" (missing "an") is shared across Aurora matchups. Aurora kit flag misfires: her passive is flagged "anti-heal target" when Riot’s text says it heals HER, and her R is flagged hardCC when the description lists only damage and slows.
